tellings.page: answer to "Could you explain the concept of the off-world download process"
tellings.quote: For example, Konstantin Tsiolkovsky on the Russian side believed that geniuses were in contact with celestial angelic beings who transmitted information for space rocket calculations.

plain: Konstantin Tsiolkovsky, the father of Russian rocketry, is said to have believed he was in touch with angelic beings, and to have written about it. The researcher Diana Pasulka tells this on the show, and in a 2023 interview she put it this way: Tsiolkovsky "believed that geniuses were in contact with celestial angelic beings who transmitted information for space rocket calculations." Michels repeats it several times, crediting Pasulka's book American Cosmic, where he says Tsiolkovsky called them "ethereal beings" talking to us through signs in the sky, and he links it to a worldview called cosmism, a kind of space religion that he says inspired the Russian space program. If true, it would mean one of the founders of spaceflight thought his ideas came from non-human minds. Tsiolkovsky's own 1928 pamphlet Unknown Intelligent Forces, in the Russian text read here, says an influence on us by living beings "like us, only more perfect" is very possible, and that some facts "speak for the intervention of some incomprehensible forces in human acts." Beings more perfect than us who act on human affairs are what the tellers call angelic. The text speaks of that influence in general rather than of a meeting of his own, so that he himself was in touch with such beings is the tellers' step, which it neither states nor rules out.

discussion.text: Tsiolkovsky's 1928 pamphlet Unknown Intelligent Forces, in the Russian Wikisource text read here (which may not be the whole pamphlet), says an influence on us of living beings "подобных нам, только более совершенных" (like us, only more perfect) is very possible, and that some facts "говорят за вмешательство каких-то непонятных сил в человеческие поступки" (speak for the intervention of some incomprehensible forces in human acts); beings more perfect than us who act on human affairs are what the tellers call angelic. The text read here speaks of that influence in general, not of a meeting of his own, so that he was himself in touch with such beings is the tellers' step, which it neither states nor excludes.
